description: Current adaptive ECG workflows plus preserved historical ReusePlan and FlowThrough profiles.
historical_profile_note: Every other profile is retained with its original stages, gates, labels, and results for historical reproduction; it cannot authorize a current ECG final stage.

profiles.ecg_grasp_reference_cache: Four serial SpMV Patents8MiB reference-consumer cells: fresh GRASP/intact favorable P-OPT, and GRASP-based FULL/FLAT diagnostics with identical complete matrix preparation and ideal runtime rank availability. Not an ECG mask or native-speed claim.
profiles.ecg_governed_first_cache: Four serial Patents 8MiB cells isolating opt-in governed-first eviction on the current NEXT record replacement rule: SpMV and PageRank, each with the option off and on and everything else identical. The control is the same-build off arm. Not a competitiveness claim against GRASP or P-OPT.
profiles.ecg_expiry_attribution_cache: Six serial Patents 8MiB cells re-reading the six attribution cells with the expiry instrument: stored line state and bounds expired against filtered progress. Instrument reading with no performance gate.
profiles.ecg_matched_baseline_cache: Serial Patents 8MiB baseline cells at the current build, on the same graphs and geometry as the governed-first cells. The SpMV pair is confirmatory, since GRASP_PAPER and POPT:UNCHARGED are already byte-identical across the 074cbf75, bb7689a9 and 2b00f213 studies. The PageRank pair is a first reading, because no matched PageRank baseline exists and POPT:UNCHARGED was never measured for PageRank on this graph. Not itself a competitiveness claim.
profiles.ecg_capacity_generality_cache: Eight serial Patents cells at 24MiB/16-way repeating the dense comparison measured at 8MiB: SpMV and PageRank, each with GRASP_PAPER, POPT:UNCHARGED, ECG base-first and ECG governed-first. One capacity change, everything else identical. Tests whether the dense result is capacity-general or specific to 8MiB; the mitigation has a reason to weaken where there is less capacity pressure, and a shrinking margin is the predicted direction.
profiles.ecg_crossover_16mb_cache: Round one of a preregistered bisection locating the capacity at which GRASP_PAPER overtakes ECG governed-first on Patents. Four cells at 16MiB/16-way: SpMV and PageRank, each with GRASP_PAPER and ECG governed-first. Only the competitor that ends the claim is sampled, so this says nothing about P-OPT or the base-first arm at intermediate capacities. The rule selecting round two is frozen in NEXT.md section ak before this runs.
profiles.ecg_crossover_20mb_cache: Round two of the preregistered bisection, at the capacity the frozen rule selected once round one showed ECG leading GRASP at 16MiB on both kernels. Four cells at 20MiB/16-way, same graph, argv and policies as round one.
profiles.ecg_pressure_gate_cache: Four serial Patents SpMV cells at 20 and 24MiB testing the opt-in pressure gate where the ungated rule loses. Governed-first is on in all four and the gate is the only variable, both arms on one binary. The gate-off arm must reproduce the crossover study exactly, since the option is meant to be neutral when disabled.
profiles.ecg_pressure_duel_cache: Thirty-two serial Patents rows at 8, 16, 20 and 24MiB/16-way testing the opt-in set-dueling pressure signal on both dense kernels. At each capacity SpMV and PageRank each run GRASP_PAPER, POPT:UNCHARGED, ECG governed-first with the gate off, and the same arm with the duel, all on one binary. Every comparison is same-binary; earlier studies are quoted only as cross-build context.
profiles.ecg_rrpv_order_cache: Thirty-two serial Patents rows at 8, 16, 20 and 24MiB/16-way testing the opt-in RRPV victim order on both dense kernels. At each capacity SpMV and PageRank each run GRASP_PAPER, POPT:UNCHARGED, ECG governed-first with the order off, and the same arm with the RRPV order, all on one binary. Every comparison is same-binary; earlier studies are quoted only as cross-build context.
profiles.ecg_kernel_census_cache: Thirty-two serial Patents rows at 8, 16, 20 and 24MiB/16-way re-running section ax's rows with the passive kernel census, which splits each kernel's transfers at its graph passes, charges every setup writeback to the segment it fell in, and reports the entry state and the exit residue. At each capacity SpMV and PageRank each run GRASP_PAPER, POPT:UNCHARGED, ECG governed-first with the RRPV order off, and the same arm with it on, all on one binary. Instrument reading, not a candidate: every comparison is same-binary and section ax is quoted only for continuity.
profiles.ecg_steady_state_cache: Thirty-two serial Patents rows at 8, 16, 20 and 24MiB/16-way that build each kernel's structures once and then run eight passes, SpMV with --repeat 8 and PageRank with -i 8, under the passive kernel census with its per-pass detail. At each capacity SpMV and PageRank each run GRASP_PAPER, POPT:UNCHARGED, ECG governed-first with the RRPV order off, and the same arm with it on, all on one binary. The gate reads passes 4 to 7; the passes are passes of one run after one construction, never independent queries.
profiles.ecg_refetch_count_cache: Eight serial Patents PageRank rows at 8, 16, 20 and 24MiB/16-way, copies of ecg_steady_state_cache's PageRank ECG jobs: ECG governed-first with the RRPV order off (the rule) and on (the arm), one build and eight passes with -i 8, under the passive kernel census with its per-pass detail and the passive DEAD-first re-fetch count. profiles.ecg_write_aware_cache: Sixteen serial Patents PageRank rows at 8, 16, 20 and 24MiB/16-way: ECG governed-first with the RRPV order off (the rule) and on (the arm), each with the written-in-place control bit off and on, one build and eight passes with -i 8, under the passive kernel census with its per-pass detail and the passive DEAD-first re-fetch count. profiles.ecg_same_binary_baselines_cache: Eight serial Patents PageRank baseline rows, GRASP_PAPER and POPT:UNCHARGED at 8, 16, 20 and 24MiB/16-way, copies of ecg_steady_state_cache's PageRank baseline jobs, run on the binary of ecg_write_aware_cache's run so that its sixteen ECG rows meet baselines from the same binary; those ECG rows are read from that run and not rerun.

ecg_grasp_reference_cache.reason: New four-run budget after the exhausted twelve-run study. Isolates graph-rank value in a fixed GRASP-base consumer before any new producer; no WINDOW/B retuning or automatic A implementation.

development_gate.additional_requirement: full strictly improves kernel transfers over fresh ordinary GRASP
development_gate.popt_comparison: report against intact P-OPT separately without weakening it

ecg_governed_first_cache.reason: Approved budget `governed-first-4`. attribution-6 measured SpMV and PageRank at 99.9% and 98.5% live bound coverage with the override firing on 44.1% and 60.8% of evictions, yet both still lose to intact P-OPT, so their deficit is in what the comparison decides rather than in the information. The base victim is not governed on 39.1% and 34.7% of their evictions, which is exactly where a governed-first rule acts and the current rule cannot. The repository's own teaching fixture specifies this order and the default rule lacks it.

development_gate.control: the same-build option-off arm, never the 074cbf75 study
development_gate.minimum_margin_scope: must hold on BOTH spmv and pr to confirm C3
development_gate.partial: a margin on one kernel only is reported as partial and must not be generalised from the winner
development_gate.reject_meaning: governed-first does not pay on the kernels where the mask is best covered; record as a negative result rather than widening it to other kernels or bases
development_gate.negative_lift: reported as a regression, never discarded
development_gate.hardware_cost: one governed bit per line, already present as WayState::property, and one comparison across ways that the cache already performs for LRU; no new storage, ports or metadata traffic
development_gate.excluded: bfs, sssp and bc are out of scope: at 8.9-26.6% live coverage their deficit is information at the moment of choice, which an ordering rule cannot supply

ecg_pressure_gate_cache.reason: Sections al and am diagnosed governed-first and the strictly-farther override as pressure heuristics applied without a pressure signal. Section an implements the signal off by default. This measures it at the two capacities where the ungated rule loses, preregistered in NEXT.md section ao.

development_gate.integrity_first: the gate-off arm must reproduce 6126909 at 20MiB and 6106480 at 24MiB exactly, zero tolerance, because the disabled path is meant to be the identical instruction sequence; any difference is VOID, is reported as an implementation defect rather than a measurement, and no other number from this run may be quoted
development_gate.arm_took: ecg_record_victim_unpressured must be a large majority of decisions on the gated arms; near zero means accepted but inert, which is void rather than negative
development_gate.formula: gated versus gate-off kernel transfers at each capacity, same binary
development_gate.helps_both: the gate removes the loss where the rule was losing and the mitigation becomes capacity-safe
development_gate.helps_one: partial; report both and do not generalise from the better one
development_gate.helps_neither: recorded as a negative result; the signal, threshold and initialisation are not retuned to rescue it and no second variant runs without a fresh budget
development_gate.regression: gated above gate-off by any margin is a regression and is reported as one
development_gate.predicted_before_running: the gate removes the regression and lands near GRASP from above, close to 5887025 at 20MiB and 5754248 at 24MiB; below GRASP would require GRASP re-measured on this binary before being claimed
development_gate.not_claimed: nothing about PageRank, 8 or 16MiB, another graph or timing, and no claim that the gate beats GRASP, whose figures here are cross-build context only

ecg_pressure_duel_cache.reason: Section ar showed the per-set counter cannot see the crossover, and section as replaces it with set dueling. Preregistered in NEXT.md section at with per-capacity predictions before any duel cell existed, and approved by the user for exactly these 32 cells.

development_gate.comparison: same binary only: every figure the gate reads comes from this profile's own rows, never from an earlier study
development_gate.integrity_first: at each capacity and kernel the four rows must carry four distinct policy labels, one binary hash and one result (SpMV result_digest, PageRank ECG-PR-RESULT score_checksum); the binary hash is each job's resolved cache_sim_benchmark_binary fingerprint, which the flow checks before and after the job, and every SpMV row's benchmark_binary_sha256 must also equal it, because PageRank rows carry no binary hash of their own; any failure voids that capacity for that kernel and is reported as a defect, not a measurement
development_gate.arm_took: on each duel row ecg_record_duel_transfers must equal the kernel memory_accesses plus llc_writebacks with zero prefetch_fills, both leader transfer counts must be positive, and the follower decisions (ecg_record_duel_follower_rule plus ecg_record_duel_follower_base) must be positive; on each gate-off row ecg_record_duel_transfers must be 0 and ecg_record_duel_selector 511; a failure is void, not negative
development_gate.formula: excess = (duel - best) / best, where best is the lower of GRASP_PAPER and the gate-off arm at that capacity and kernel
development_gate.capacity_safe: excess <= 0.01 at all four capacities for a kernel
development_gate.partial: excess <= 0.01 at some capacities only; report every capacity and do not generalise from the ones that pass
development_gate.not_safe: excess > 0.01 at every capacity; recorded as a negative result, and the leader count, leader slots, selector width, initial value and transfer definition are not retuned to rescue it
development_gate.regression: a duel row above both GRASP_PAPER and the gate-off arm at any capacity is a regression and is reported as one
development_gate.beats_both: excess < -0.01 would be a surprise; it is reported with the follower split and winner changes that explain it and is not generalised beyond this graph
development_gate.competitive_report: the duel's signed margin against GRASP_PAPER and POPT:UNCHARGED at every capacity and kernel, same binary, as (baseline - duel) / baseline so that a positive margin means the duel moves fewer transfers, the convention of every earlier study; a margin under 1% is reported as thin and never generalised
development_gate.continuity: the gate-off, GRASP_PAPER and POPT:UNCHARGED rows are compared with the earlier studies and reported as exact or with their difference; this is not gating, because the duel enlarged CacheLevel and a fixture showed a heap-layout shift moving SpMV transfers across builds, so the verdict rests on same-binary rows only
development_gate.hardware_cost: one 10-bit saturating selector per LLC, a 6-bit set-index comparison naming 2 leader sets in every 64, and one increment or decrement on transfers the cache already performs; no per-set or per-line state, no new ports and no metadata traffic
development_gate.predicted_before_running: each kernel pays about 1/64 of the gap between its two pure policies, the leader sets running the losing one: excess about 0.4% at 8MiB, 0.1-0.2% at 16MiB and 0.1% or less at 20 and 24MiB; followers mostly on the rule at 8 and 16MiB and mostly relaxed at 20 and 24MiB, with PageRank at 20MiB least certain because its two policies differ by 1.07%; the SpMV margin over POPT:UNCHARGED at 8MiB, 0.88% cross-build, thins to about 0.5%
development_gate.not_claimed: nothing about BFS, SSSP or BC, another graph, timing, gem5 or Sniper, which refuse the gate; the duel's ceiling is the better of the base policy and the rule, so where it follows GRASP_PAPER any margin over POPT:UNCHARGED is GRASP's and is not credited to the record rule

ecg_rrpv_order_cache.reason: Section au found that above 8MiB the rule never compares the record's bound, so its least-recent ungoverned order sets the crossover, and section av removes recency from every ECG victim decision with an opt-in RRPV order built on the GRASP state record mode already keeps. Preregistered in NEXT.md section aw with per-capacity predictions before any arm cell existed, and approved by the user for exactly these 32 rows.

development_gate.comparison: same binary only: every figure the gate reads comes from this profile's own rows, never from an earlier study
development_gate.integrity_first: at each capacity and kernel the four rows must carry four distinct policy labels, one binary hash and one result (SpMV result_digest, PageRank ECG-PR-RESULT score_checksum), zero prefetch_fills and identical kernel access counts; the binary hash is each job's resolved cache_sim_benchmark_binary fingerprint, which the flow checks before and after the job, and every SpMV row's benchmark_binary_sha256 must also equal it, because PageRank rows carry no binary hash of their own; any failure voids that capacity for that kernel and is reported as a defect, not a measurement
development_gate.arm_took: on each arm row ecg_record_victim_rrpv_ordered must equal ecg_record_victim_decisions and be positive, ecg_record_victim_base_lru must be 0, ecg_record_victim_rrpv_changed must be positive, and each PageRank arm log must carry [ECG-PR-RRPV-ORDER hot_percent=50 boundary=capacity]; on each rule row ecg_record_victim_rrpv_ordered and ecg_record_victim_rrpv_changed must be 0, and ecg_record_victim_base_lru must be 0 on SpMV and equal base_no_future plus base_not_governed plus base_kept plus overridden on PageRank, which section au measured as 0 above 8MiB; a failure is void, not negative
development_gate.formula: lift = (rule - arm) / rule per kernel and capacity, where rule is the governed-first row with the order off and arm is the same row with the RRPV order
development_gate.confirmed: safe at 8 and 16MiB and improving at both 20 and 24MiB for that kernel
development_gate.partial: short of confirmed with no regression; report every capacity and do not generalise from the ones that pass
development_gate.negative: lift < 0.010 at both 20 and 24MiB with no regression; recorded as a negative result, and the scan, tiers, mask and ageing are not retuned to rescue it
development_gate.regression: lift < -0.005 at any capacity is a regression and is reported as one
development_gate.surprise: lift > 0.05 anywhere is reported with the decision split that explains it and is not generalised beyond this graph

stages.name: 60_gem5_proposal_reuse_bind_o3
stages.notes: Mechanism-only gate with a width-unmatched 8-byte non-FlowThrough ReusePlan semantic anchor plus transport-matched 4-byte FlowThrough lru_only and epoch_first arms. roi_matrix forces capped 2048-event ReuseBind and FlowThrough traces; every FlowThrough row must attest only 4-byte request-flag record loads, exact same-line O3 ReuseBind Request acceptance, and multiple nonzero record-derived plans. All three rows must match PageRank semantics. The anchor is not a FlowThrough control, and this proves existence and binding rather than request-count or performance coverage.

stages.name: 61_gem5_csr_transport_cit_i1
stages.notes: Single bounded transport calibration. Per-array x requestor LLC attribution must reconcile exactly before comparing the ReusePlan-LRU FlowThrough control with its same-job LRU denominator; no broader stage is unlocked by this run. Scope is single-core CPU data/instruction demand traffic with prefetching disabled. Unclassified-other CPU-data demand misses must remain at or below 2%. The graph is symmetrized, so incoming and outgoing CSR edge/index storage aliases; directed-graph attribution requires exporting the outgoing index range separately.

stages.name: 62_cache_sim_matched_policy_replay
stages.notes: Every ReusePlan arm uses identical 4-byte FlowThrough transport. T-OPT retains the common warm prefix to establish cache state, marks the cache-stat reset as ROI start, fingerprints only ROI requests, and counts oracle hits/misses only in the ROI suffix; next-use optimization still sees the full warm+ROI sequence. The runner requires the exact six-arm ReusePlan roster to produce one identical post-L2 address/class/read-write fingerprint and Belady result, checks ROI trace accesses equal measured LLC accesses, and requires the oracle floor not exceed measured misses before comparing victim rules. LRU and native GRASP are reference rows with explicitly independent oracle-group hashes.

stages.name: 63_gem5_shortcircuit_cit_i1
stages.notes: Single replay-promoted timing cell. The 4-byte compact record is fail-closed, per-array attribution must validate, FlowThrough records must cold-miss exactly once per line, and all comparisons use one local LRU denominator. This is one n18 sample point, not a general performance claim.

stages.name: 64_gem5_epoch_attribution_cit_i1
stages.notes: Decisive epoch-efficacy cell. All ReusePlan arms use identical 4-byte compact FlowThrough transport. Resettable replacement-policy counters quantify request validity, live stamped ways, context mismatches, zero-stamped selections, stamped victims selected through an epoch-capable path, epoch-decisive selections from a metadata-disabled shadow decision, and victim-way concentration. Eligibility is a liveness check; only the decisive counter shows that epoch metadata changed a victim. Compare RRIP-first against GRASP-only for the combined RRIP path, and epoch-first against the records-first/property-LRU arm for an exact runtime epoch contrast. Do not infer a future-reference benefit from RRIP behavior alone.

stages.name: 65_gem5_rrip_epoch_attribution_cit_i1
stages.notes: Applied positional counterfactual. RRIP-no-epoch keeps the exact RRIP eligibility gate, records-first selection, insertion, transport, and guest work of RRIP-first while replacing epoch distance with fixed set order. This stage measures epoch-path versus positional selection; stage 66 supplies the neutral property-recency epoch-information test. GRASP-only and transport-LRU remain local decomposition controls.

stages.name: 66_gem5_rrip_recency_attribution_cit_i1
stages.notes: Neutral epoch-information test. All three ReusePlan arms share RRIP eligibility, aging, records-first selection, insertion, compact transport, and guest work. The positional control chooses the first property candidate; the neutral control chooses the oldest property candidate; RRIP-first uses epoch distance. Epoch information is useful only if RRIP-first materially beats the recency control.

stages.name: 67_cache_sim_future_admission_i1
stages.notes: Signal gate, not a novelty claim. The recency-admission treatment and recency control differ only in future-distance admission/refresh. The future-tier arm tests the intended combined mask at eviction: future distance first, carried GRASP tier on epoch ties, then recency. The combined-admission arm averages tier and future RRPV. The admission+epoch arm completes the admission x eviction interaction. All ReusePlan arms share compact records and FlowThrough; LRU and GRASP receive the same generic structural FlowThrough opportunity. scripts/experiments/ecg/analysis/future_admission_gate.py compares each treatment to its named matched control using the unweighted geometric mean of per-graph ratios. Promote to gem5 only if a treatment reaches at most 0.97 for both LLC misses and total off-chip traffic, with neither metric above 1.02 on any graph. P-OPT/Hawkeye comparison remains mandatory before any novelty claim.

stages.name: 68_cache_sim_temporal_discrimination_i1
stages.notes: Mechanism discrimination, not a performance claim. Both symmetrized graphs derive from 65,536-vertex, degree-eight directed inputs and have identical serialized counts and degree sequences. Clustered readers are adjacent in the preserved vertex sweep; spread readers are separated across the graph. GRASP receives the same degree distribution in both cells. This stage isolates eviction ranking; admission is evaluated on the real-graph stage because clustered reuse is absorbed by private caches and produces no LLC admission updates. A future-mask policy must respond to the timing change while preserving exact semantics and symmetric FlowThrough.

stages.name: 69_gem5_temporal_admission_i1
stages.notes: Mechanism-only matched O3 test on the directed spread-reader graph. Both rows use the corrected builder-v2 mask, compact 4-byte FlowThrough records, request-bound ReuseBind, RRIP eligibility/aging, and property-recency eviction. Only future-distance admission/refresh changes. Array-attribution schema 2 separately accounts incoming traversal and outgoing-degree CSR offsets. One architectural record sweep is required; O3 replay may add at most 0.5% record-line misses, while a second sweep remains fail-closed. This synthetic control cannot support a general performance or novelty claim.

stages.name: 69b_cache_sim_online_admission_i1

The gate failed because those colors were not representative. The profile is blocked so current generation-2 code cannot silently overwrite that evidence. Use the tracked generation-2 color-sweep flow and its separate analyzer.
